title: PM Modi creates exam reform task force after minister resigns over leaks

origin.headline: PM Modi creates exam reform task force after minister resigns over leaks

backstory.body:
Cadera Edu reported that in May 2015, Haryana Police uncovered a cheating scam during the All India Pre-Medical Test. Candidates used Bluetooth vests and micro-SIM devices to receive answers during the exam. On June 15, 2015, Cadera Edu reported that the Supreme Court of India cancelled the entire 2015 All India Pre-Medical Test following the discovery of this high-tech electronic cheating ring. The Supreme Court ordered a fresh test. On July 24, 2016, Cadera Edu reported that Uttarakhand Police arrested several individuals linked to an inter-state syndicate accused of selling leaked NEET Phase II question papers.

Indian Express reported that the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024 was introduced in the 17th Lok Sabha on February 5, 2024, to combat paper leaks and examination fraud. Indian Express reported that the Lok Sabha passed the bill on February 6, 2024. Indian Express reported that the Rajya Sabha passed the bill on February 9, 2024. On May 5, 2024, the National Testing Agency conducted the NEET-UG 2024 examination across India amid immediate allegations of paper leaks and subsequent arrests in Bihar. Wikipedia reported that the exam was conducted for 2.4 million candidates amid paper leak allegations in Patna and Gujarat.

On June 4, 2024, the National Testing Agency declared the results of NEET-UG 2024, which sparked controversy over an unprecedented 67 candidates obtaining perfect scores. On June 11, 2024, Law Notes reported that the Supreme Court observed that the sanctity of the NEET-UG 2024 exam was affected. Law Notes reported that the court demanded answers from the National Testing Agency while refusing to stay counseling. On June 13, 2024, Deccan Chronicle reported that Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stated there was no evidence of a paper leak in NEET-UG 2024 and defended the credibility of the agency. On the same day, Law Notes reported that the Supreme Court allowed the cancellation of scorecards for 1,563 NEET-UG 2024 candidates who were awarded grace marks and ordered a re-test. On June 19, 2024, Indian Express reported that the Ministry of Education cancelled the UGC-NET 2024 exam after learning that the integrity of the test was compromised.

India Today reported that on June 22, 2024, the Union Ministry of Education formed a High-Level Committee of Experts chaired by Dr. K. Radhakrishnan to recommend examination reforms for the National Testing Agency after the NEET-UG paper leaks. On the same day, The Statesman reported that the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 officially came into force across India. On June 23, 2024, the National Testing Agency reconducted the NEET-UG 2024 examination for the 1,563 candidates who had previously received grace marks. On June 28, 2024, hrw.org reported that activist Sonam Wangchuk began a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar to demand accountability for exam paper leaks and youth unemployment. On June 30, 2024, deccanchronicle.com reported that the agency declared the official results for the NEET-UG 2024 re-test.

On July 6, 2024, deccanchronicle.com reported that medical admission counselling for undergraduate MBBS and BDS courses officially commenced across India. On July 20, 2024, the Cockroach Janta Party organized a 'Chalo Sansad' march in New Delhi, where police used force and tear gas against student demonstrators. On July 21, 2024, aa.com.tr reported that Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that 13 people had been jailed for involvement in the paper leak as protests continued in New Delhi. On July 23, 2024, Wikipedia reported that the Supreme Court found 155 students benefited from the NEET-UG 2024 leak. Wikipedia reported that the court declined to order a full re-examination due to a lack of evidence of systemic failure. On August 2, 2024, Indian Express reported that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan declared that the Supreme Court verdict rejected opposition propaganda and vindicated the government on NEET-UG 2024. India Today reported that in August 2024, the Supreme Court widened the mandate of the Radhakrishnan committee. On October 21, 2024, the K. Radhakrishnan Committee submitted its final report on National Testing Agency reforms containing 101 recommendations to the Union Ministry of Education.

Vajiram & Ravi reported that a High-Powered Steering Committee chaired by Dr. K. Radhakrishnan was constituted on November 14, 2024, to monitor the execution of examination reforms. In December 2024, ndtv.com reported that Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan announced to Parliament that the National Testing Agency would limit its role strictly to entrance examinations starting in 2025.

Hindustan Times reported that in January 2025, the National Testing Agency introduced enhanced security protocols including Aadhaar authentication and repeat biometric checks during the JEE (Main) examination. India Today reported in April 2025 that the Union Ministry of Education made the Radhakrishnan committee report public. indiatoday.in also reported in April 2025 that the Ministry of Education publicly released the Radhakrishnan Committee report on examination reforms.

On October 13, 2025, the Parliament of India reported that the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education adopted its draft 371st report evaluating autonomous bodies under higher education. On December 8, 2025, India Today reported that the 371st Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, chaired by Digvijaya Singh, was tabled in the Rajya Sabha. PRS Legislative Research reported that this 371st Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education was tabled in the Rajya Sabha, criticizing the performance of the National Testing Agency and urging reliance on in-house capacity.

On May 3, 2026, the National Testing Agency conducted the NEET-UG 2026 examination across the country for over 2.27 million aspirants seeking admission to undergraduate medical and dental courses. Wikipedia reported that reports emerged following the exam that a handwritten guess paper had been leaked beforehand. A teacher from a coaching center in Sikar, Rajasthan, discovered a handwritten guess paper that was identical to the actual NEET UG 2026 exam paper. timesofindia.indiatimes.com reported that a handwritten copy of the NEET UG 2026 question paper was scanned and converted into PDF files in Rajasthan by the father of an aspirant and then circulated to students in coaching centers.

vibesofindia.com reported that chemistry teacher Shashikant Suthar reported to police in Sikar, Rajasthan, on May 4, 2026, that a handwritten guess paper matched the actual NEET-UG 2026 questions. vibesofindia.com also reported that the teacher who discovered the paper leak initially approached the Udyog Nagar police station to report the issue but did not file a written complaint. matchtocollege.com reported that initial reports and social media virality regarding alleged paper leaks from specific examination centers in various states began on May 6, 2026. On May 7, 2026, vibesofindia.com reported that the teacher officially lodged a complaint with the National Testing Agency, providing a 60-page handwritten PDF containing chemistry and biology questions that matched the actual exam. Vibes of India reported that chemistry teacher Shashikant Suthar sent a formal complaint to the National Testing Agency detailing a 60-page PDF matching questions in the NEET-UG 2026 exam.

matchtocollege.com reported that the National Testing Agency initially denied a widespread leak of the NEET UG 2026 paper on May 9, 2026. On May 12, 2026, the NEET UG 2026 examination was officially cancelled by the National Testing Agency following investigations that revealed significant overlaps between a pre-circulated guess paper and the actual question paper. youtube.com reported that National Testing Agency Director General Abhishek Singh stated that while the entire paper was never available on Telegram or any other channel, some questions did match. The Central Bureau of Investigation officially took over the investigation into the NEET UG 2026 paper leak. Wikipedia reported that the National Testing Agency officially cancelled NEET-UG 2026, announced a re-examination, and transferred the leak investigation to the Central Bureau of Investigation. Telangana Today reported that a letter petition was filed in the Supreme Court on May 13, 2026, requesting a court-monitored investigation into repeated NEET paper leaks and the replacement of the National Testing Agency.

wikipedia.org reported that on May 15, 2026, the National Testing Agency announced that the re-examination for NEET UG 2026 would take place on June 21, 2026, and promised students refunds of their application fees. Economic Times reported that Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made oral observations on May 15, 2026, comparing certain unemployed youth and social media activists to cockroaches and parasites. Economic Times reported that Abhijeet Dipke launched the Cockroach Janta Party movement on social media on May 16, 2026, in response to Chief Justice Surya Kant's remarks. time.com reported that the Cockroach Janta Party established its demands on May 16, 2026, including compensation for student suicides, legislative oversight, gender equity, independent media, and electoral reforms.

On May 22, 2026, Manisha Sanjay Havaldar, a school headmistress and National Testing Agency subject expert, was arrested for allegedly leaking the physics question paper. SuperKalam reported that on May 25, 2026, the Supreme Court requested a status report regarding the implementation of the Radhakrishnan Committee's recommendations for National Testing Agency reforms. The Hindu reported that on May 29, 2026, the Supreme Court stated that NEET-UG paper leaks traumatised entire families and questioned the National Testing Agency's operational credibility.

hrw.org reported that protests began in June 2026 to demand accountability for mismanagement of medical entrance examinations. time.com reported that the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party began organizing protests in June 2026. Economic Times reported that the Cockroach Janta Party held its first physical demonstration at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on June 6, 2026, demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. aljazeera.com reported that on June 19, 2026, Abhijeet Dipke made a social media post asking what if all cockroaches came together, which sparked the creation of the Cockroach Janta Party. Hindustan Times reported that on June 19, 2026, Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke published an open letter to Prime Minister Modi demanding 1 crore rupees in compensation for families of students who died by suicide. The NEET UG 2026 re-examination was conducted on June 21, 2026. Economic Times reported that activist Sonam Wangchuk began an indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar on June 28, 2026, demanding Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and examination reforms.

On May 3, 2026, over 2.2 million medical aspirants took the nationwide NEET-UG 2026 entrance examination conducted by the National Testing Agency. Vibes of India reported that on May 4, 2026, a coaching centre teacher in Sikar, Rajasthan, approached the Udyog Nagar police station after finding a handwritten guess paper that closely matched the NEET-UG 2026 exam. vibesofindia.com reported that on May 7, 2026, Shashikant Suthar submitted a formal complaint to the National Testing Agency along with a 60-page handwritten PDF of leaked chemistry and biology questions. On May 12, 2026, the National Testing Agency officially cancelled the NEET-UG 2026 examination following evidence of paper leaks and widespread irregularities. The probe into the leak was handed over to the Central Bureau of Investigation. Wikipedia reported that on May 15, 2026, the National Testing Agency scheduled the NEET-UG 2026 re-examination for June 21, 2026. On June 21, 2026, the National Testing Agency reconducted the nationwide NEET-UG 2026 re-examination for affected undergraduate medical candidates. Human Rights Watch reported that on June 28, 2026, activist Sonam Wangchuk began a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi to advocate for student rights and education reforms.

Caderaedu.com reported that the result of the NEET UG 2026 re-examination was declared on July 16, 2026. On July 18, 2026, activist Sonam Wangchuk was forcibly removed from Jantar Mantar and admitted to a public hospital after 26 days of a hunger strike. On July 20, 2026, police and security forces used tear gas, batons, and allegedly pellet guns against student protesters marching towards Parliament in Delhi, resulting in numerous injuries. During the Delhi demonstrations, 19-year-old student Sahil Lochab sustained pellet-like injuries to his right eye, face, neck, chest, and shoulder. An RAF jawan was photographed holding what appeared to be a pellet gun during the protests. Newindianexpress.com reported that one RAF personnel fired seven rounds from his pellet gun during the student demonstrations. Amnesty.org reported that authorities suspended metro services and mobile internet in Delhi during the protests.

On July 21, 2026, Sahil Lochab underwent surgery at the AIIMS Jai Prakash Narayan Apex Trauma Centre to remove pellets and repair his injured eye. Doctors informed his family that there was only a 1% chance of vision returning to his right eye due to pupil damage. Human Rights Watch reported that political opposition leaders criticized the police crackdown on student protests, calling the government insensitive and authoritarian. Human Rights Watch also reported that Delhi police temporarily detained several top opposition leaders after a nearly three-hour protest in front of Prime Minister Modi’s residence. Hindustan Times reported that a 23-year-old NEET aspirant died by suicide in Dehradun due to dissatisfaction over excelling in her studies.

On July 22, 2026, article-14.com reported that Sahil Lochab underwent his first operation to remove particles from pellet wounds in his shoulder, chest, and face. The Wire reported that an Outlook reporter sustained multiple puncture wounds on his arm from a weapon matching the description of a pellet gun during the protests. Hindustan Times reported that a 17-year-old student died after allegedly falling from the sixth floor of a residential building in Ahmedabad while preparing for the NEET re-test. On July 23, 2026, Indian Express reported that doctors offered some reassurance to Sahil Lochab's family that the chances of his vision improving might be increasing, though his prognosis remains guarded. Human Rights Watch reported that Indian security forces used tear gas and batons to suppress largely peaceful student and youth protests in New Delhi on July 20. Times of India reported that a special fast-track court was constituted at Delhi's Rouse Avenue Courts to exclusively handle offenses under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

On July 25, 2026, Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister following student protests over the NEET UG 2026 paper leak. Newsgram.com reported that Pradhan stated in a public letter that his resignation was to protect the future of students and prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the protests. Youth activist group Cockroach Janta Party called off its protests after the government accepted its demands, including Pradhan's resignation and dropping legal measures against student demonstrators. Al Jazeera reported that Health Minister JP Nadda stated that the central government would soon fix the compensation amount for the families of children who died by suicide after question leaks.

On July 26, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the formation of a high-powered task force led by Nandan Nilekani to make India's examination system leak-proof and recommend structural and technological reforms. The Hindu reported that Union Minister Pralhad Joshi officially took charge of the Ministry of Education at Kartavya Bhavan. On July 27, 2026, Channel NewsAsia reported that Prime Minister Modi stated new legislation tightening laws and penalties for exam paper leaks will be introduced in Parliament. The Union government introduced the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha. Hindustan Times reported that Rahul Gandhi sent a letter to Home Minister Amit Shah demanding accountability for police actions against student protesters in Delhi on July 20. Times of India reported that following campaigns over paper leaks, the newly formed E20 Janta Party demanded the government provide consumers an option to buy 100% petrol and called for the resignation of minister Nitin Gadkari. Indian Express reported that Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy announced the state assembly will pass a resolution in August to recommend lowering the minimum Lok Sabha candidacy age to 21 from 25. The Cockroach Janta Party warned of resuming protests, stating there was a breach of agreement regarding no police action against protesters.

Cadera Edu reported that the National Testing Agency declared the official results for the June 21 Re-NEET examination on July 16, 2026. Two days later, on July 18, Delhi Police forcefully moved activist Sonam Wangchuk from Jantar Mantar to a hospital on the 21st day of his hunger strike.

Protests escalated on July 20 as thousands of student demonstrators marched towards Parliament under the Cockroach Janta Party banner. Delhi Police used batons and tear gas to block the marching students. Al Jazeera reported that Delhi Police used tear gas and batons against the Cockroach Janta Party student demonstrators, resulting in widespread injuries. Overall, police clashed with thousands of student protesters marching towards Parliament, leaving more than 100 demonstrators and security officers injured.

Following the violence, Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh held negotiations with representatives of the Cockroach Janta Party on July 22, according to the Economic Times. On July 23, The Hindu reported that the Delhi High Court designated Judge Anu Grover Baliga to head a special fast-track court at Rouse Avenue Courts for handling paper leak cases. The Economic Times also reported that activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike on July 23 after receiving government assurances regarding student protection and compensation. On July 24, Law Notes reported that the Supreme Court agreed to hear petitions alleging police brutality against students protesting the NEET paper leaks.

The mounting protests led to high-level political developments on July 25. Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from his cabinet post following weeks of widespread youth-led protests over exam leaks. Wikipedia reported that Pradhan submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Following government assurances and an agreement to key demands, including dropping charges against student demonstrators, the Cockroach Janta Party called off its 36-day nationwide protest. Daily Sun reported that the group announced the end of its nationwide agitation during a joint press conference after the government accepted its key demands.

On July 26, the Indian Express reported that Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy announced the state assembly would pass a resolution recommending lowering the minimum age for Lok Sabha members to 21. On the same day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a high-powered task force headed by Nandan Nilekani to revamp the national examination system.

Legal proceedings and political debate continued on July 27. Timesofindia.indiatimes.com reported that the Supreme Court of India began hearing petitions concerning alleged police excesses during protests related to the NEET UG 2026 paper leak. At Delhi's Rouse Avenue Courts, timesofindia.indiatimes.com reported that the fast-track court adjourned the bail pleas of Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal to August 3 because no legal representative from the Central Bureau of Investigation appeared. Timesofindia.indiatimes.com also reported that the court directed the director of prosecution to appoint a public prosecutor for the Central Bureau of Investigation. Thestatesman.com reported that the Congress party criticized the Central Bureau of Investigation for failing to send a legal representative to the inaugural hearing of the fast-track court. Meanwhile, newindianexpress.com reported that the Bihar government indicated plans to withdraw cases against those booked during NEET paper leak protests.

Despite the earlier end to protests, student leaders maintained pressure on the government on July 27. Rediff.com reported that the Cockroach Janta Party demanded a written agreement from the government regarding the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters. Rediff reported that the group warned it would resume protests if the Centre failed to provide a written agreement withdrawing criminal cases against demonstrators. The Cockroach Janta Party warned it would resume nationwide protests if the government failed to deliver a formal written commitment to withdraw all police cases against demonstrators. On July 28, SC Observer reported that the Supreme Court ordered the immediate release of all detained minor student protesters without criminal antecedents and restrained authorities from taking coercive action.
